subtype: Approach: earning extra by doing jobs at home [Action]
passage:
Preetam: Papa, can I earn some money? Otherwise the toy takes me twelve weeks.
Papa: Doing what?
Preetam: Washing the car every Sunday. For Rs 10.
Papa: Hmm. Bucket, soap, dry with the cloth, and no water on the seats.
Preetam: Deal!
Sabina: Wait, Preetam, if you earn Rs 10 extra, that's eight weeks instead of twelve.
Preetam: Really, Didi?
Sabina: I did the sums on the fridge board. Eight.
Preetam: Then I start this Sunday. Mummy, where's the big bucket?
Mummy: Under the sink. Don't forget the tyres.

qa.q: How much does Papa pay for washing the car?
qa.a: Papa pays Rs 10 for washing the car.

qa.q: What does Preetam want when asking Papa about earning money?
qa.a: Preetam wants to shorten the wait for the toy by earning extra, and is eager, as seen in starting this Sunday.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Preetam use as well, and why?
qa.a: Preetam could set a smaller first target or ask relatives for money at a festival. Either could shorten the wait while the Sunday job keeps adding up.

qa.q: How does Sabina see Preetam's plan?
qa.a: Sabina did the sums on the fridge board and is happy to share the result, which shows an older sister who wants the plan to work.

grounding: Preetam asks the parents whether washing the car on Sundays can earn extra money, which shortens the wait from twelve weeks to eight.

subtype: Approach: earning extra by doing jobs at home [Action]
passage: Last year I wanted a Rs 240 kite-making kit, the big one with the spinning reel. My pocket money was Rs 20 a week, so I worked it out: twelve weeks. That felt like forever. So one Saturday I asked Papa and my mother, Sharmila, 'If I wash the car every Sunday, can I get Rs 10?' Papa looked at Ma. Ma said, 'Properly, with the bucket, not just splashing.' Every Sunday morning I washed it: soap, rinse, dry with the old towel, even the wheels. Rs 20 plus Rs 10 made Rs 30 a week. I did the maths again. Eight weeks! I got the kit four weeks sooner, and Papa said, 'Tarun beta, this car has never been so clean.'

qa.q: How much did Tarun earn for each car wash?
How did Tarun feel about waiting twelve weeks?
qa.a: Twelve weeks felt like forever, so Tarun was impatient and keen to find a quicker way.

qa.q: Why was asking his parents first a good step?
qa.a: They agreed on the job and how it should be done, like washing properly with the bucket, so the extra money was fair and clear.

qa.q: How did Papa see the Sunday washes?
qa.a: Papa said the car had never been so clean, so he seemed pleased with the arrangement.

grounding: Shows a boy asking his parents to earn Rs 10 for washing the car on Sundays, cutting his saving time from twelve weeks to eight.

subtype: Approach: earning extra by doing jobs at home [Action]
passage: Note in the family diary, Sunday. Last week Tejas asked if he could earn Rs 10 by washing the car every Sunday. He's saving for a Rs 240 cricket set like his friend Irfan's, and on his Rs 20 a week it would take twelve weeks. We agreed, on condition that he does it properly. This morning he was up at seven with the bucket, the old towel and the brush for the tyres. It took him forty minutes. He came in soaked, held out his hand for the Rs 10, and then wrote in his little notebook: 'Rs 30 a week now. 8 weeks!' I've put a star on the calendar eight Sundays from today.

qa.q: How long did the car wash take Tejas?
How did Tejas seem to feel when he wrote '8 weeks!'?
qa.a: He seemed excited and proud that his own work had cut the wait from twelve weeks to eight.
Tejas asked first and agreed a clear job with his family, then kept to it, which shortened his wait.

qa.q: How does the note-writer see Tejas's effort?
qa.a: The note-writer notices him up at seven doing it properly and backs the goal by starring the calendar.

grounding: Illustrates a boy agreeing with his family to earn Rs 10 by washing the car each Sunday, shortening his wait from twelve weeks to eight.
